title: UDLM Class artifact — the scoped-Class authoring layer
description: Meta-schema for a Class artifact (registry/classes/*.yaml), the authoring layer of the scoped resource-type Class hierarchy (ADR-038). A Class carries the FULL definition surface — elements, outputs, relationships (consumer-declared), immutable, adopts, and (type tier) context — closing #323 so the compiled flat spec is complete, not a subset. A Class composes SharedDataElements (`$defs.shared_data_element`) at one scope tier — Base (`Category`), Type (`Category.Type`), or Provider (`Category.Type.Provider`) — each `extends` its parent under the Liskov invariant (add or refine, never contradict). Classes become the authoring layer; a generator compiles each Type Class down to the flat resource-type-spec shape consumers read today (`--check`-gated, no downstream break — realization-plan P0). An element's scope position IS its portability (ADR-038 §3), so the realized `portability` block derives from where an instance's populated elements sit rather than being asserted. Part of the UDLM spec, versioned on the SPEC axis. Status: ADR-038 is Proposed pending the engineering pass (#217); this shape inherits that status and executes the decided model (realization-plan).

metadata.description: EXAMPLE Provider Class — not canonical. Per the ADR-038 authorship ruling, Provider Classes are provider-authored and reach canonical standing through the DCM contribution lifecycle; this file demonstrates the grammar for the class named illustratively throughout ADR-038. OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt) Provider Class for the Compute.VM Type Class. Carries only what is meaningful when the VM lands on this provider: the target namespace (the canonical ADR-016 example of a provider-required field that lives off the portable type), instancetype/preference selection, run and eviction strategy, storage-class and boot-source mechanics, secondary-network attachments, and the GPU-passthrough / SR-IOV elements the Compute.VirtualMachine flat spec explicitly parks for the Provider tier. Elements are proposed pending a grounding pass against a live VirtualMachine custom resource (deferred — OpenShift Virtualization not currently installed in the reference estate).

elements.description: Target OpenShift namespace for the VirtualMachine object. The request-realization enrichment step fills this from a governed layer via post-placement policy (ADR-024); a consumer never names it in portable intent.

VirtualMachineClusterInstancetype name (for example u1.medium) selecting the provider's sizing bundle. When set, the provider derives vCPU and memory from the instancetype; policy validates it against the portable cpu and memory elements rather than letting the two diverge.
VirtualMachineClusterPreference name (for example fedora, windows.10) supplying guest-OS-tuned device and feature defaults.
Desired run posture of the VirtualMachine, mapped to the KubeVirt runStrategy values Always, Halted, Manual, RerunOnFailure and Once.

OpenShift StorageClass backing the VM's root and data volumes. Placement selects it from the provider's advertised classes; the consumer's portable intent speaks in storage_tier, never in a provider class name.
Boot image mechanics for this provider: a containerDisk image reference or the name of a DataVolume/PVC boot source in the target namespace.
Multus NetworkAttachmentDefinition references for secondary interfaces (for example an OVN localnet to a VLAN). Ordered; the primary pod network is implicit and never listed.
Behavior when the scheduler must vacate the node, mapped to the KubeVirt evictionStrategy values LiveMigrate, LiveMigrateIfPossible, None and External.
Host GPU devices passed through to the guest, by permitted device name. This is one of the two elements the Compute.VirtualMachine flat spec deliberately excludes as Provider-Class surface (ADR-038).
SR-IOV network references for direct virtual-function interfaces. The second element the Compute.VirtualMachine flat spec deliberately excludes as Provider-Class surface (ADR-038).

vmi_phase.description: EXAMPLE — provider-scope output: the KubeVirt VirtualMachineInstance phase as last reported (Running, Succeeded, Failed).

relationships.description: EXAMPLE — consumer-declared: this provider class consumes the advertised storage class it schedules volumes onto (declared HERE, on the consumer — the target never lists its consumers).

adopts.role: EXAMPLE — the provider-native construct this class naturalizes to; adopted by reference, never re-expressed.

metadata.description: EXAMPLE composite definition — the combining artifact in the class system: a type-tier class composing OTHER classes by reference. The catalog item is a projection rendered implementation-side (one declaration, two projections: registration presents it, the catalog offers it); constituents never enter a compiled flat spec — a composite expands at request time.

$id.description: Canonical identifier: https://udlm.dev/registry/udlm/<spec>/class/<ClassName>/<version>. ClassName is the dotted Class name (Compute, Compute.VM, Compute.VM.OCPVirt). A new MAJOR mints a new $id; the uuid never changes (ADR-051).

conforms_to.description: SPEC-axis binding: the UDLM spec major.minor this Class is written against.

uuid.description: Frozen identity (ADR-051): never changes, never reused; a content change bumps `version`, not this.

record_type.description: Dispatch key: this document is a Class artifact (validate.py dispatches it to class.schema.json).

class.description: The scope tier. `base` = Category scope (single-segment name); `type` = Category.Type; `provider` = Category.Type.Provider (provider-authored). MUST match the segment-count of `resource_type`.

resource_type.description: The dotted Class name — one segment for a Base Class (`Compute`), two for a Type Class (`Compute.VM`), three for a Provider Class (`Compute.VM.OCPVirt`). Every element's `scope` MUST equal this.

parent.description: The parent Class this one `extends` (the dotted name one segment shorter). Required for `type` and `provider`; absent for `base` (a Base Class has no parent). The child adds or refines the parent's elements, never contradicts them (the Liskov invariant — enforced by validate_registry's Liskov gate).

version.description: Semver on the CONTENT axis (VERSIONING.md + the ADR-051 publish law). Narrowing an element's scope is breaking even with no shape change (ADR-045/UC-009).

family.description: The entity family this Class belongs to (entities/*.md). The Process family may lead class-system adoption (automation intent, realization-plan priority signal).

status.description: Lifecycle status of the Class definition itself.

adopts.description: External standards this Class adopts by reference (T5) — items ARE the flat spec's `adopted_standard_ref` ($ref — one shape, single source). Compile: pass-through, union down the chain, deduplicated by standard+standard_name. A Base Class adoption is inherited by every descendant's compiled spec (#323).

metadata.description: Authoring metadata (author/authority, timestamps, provenance). The provider- or org-authority under which a non-canonical Class is held lives here (ADR-038 authorship & domain).

elements.description: The SharedDataElements this Class contributes at its scope — the composable units (ADR-038 §2). A Type Class's compiled flat spec is its elements plus every ancestor's, landed under `spec.properties`.

coverage.description: Spec-completeness link (rule-36 — CONTRIBUTING 'a spec travels with its story'): the Use Case(s) and flow(s) that exercise this Class. A Class is its own worked example, so `examples` is not required here; spec_coverage.py resolves each referent and fails on a dangling one in --strict.

use_cases.description: UC handle(s) or use-cases/ path(s) that exercise this Class.

examples.description: Optional additional worked example(s) beyond the Class artifact itself.

flows.description: docs/flows/ doc(s) that place this Class in a lifecycle.

outputs.description: Typed Realized-state outputs this Class publishes (E2), keyed by output name — a JSON-Schema fragment per output, same shape as the flat spec's `outputs`. Scoped like elements: any tier may declare (a Provider Class declaring provider-specific outputs is exactly the intended use, #323); the declaring Class IS the scope. Compile: merged down the chain, nearer Class overrides by name; a redeclare MUST refine (the Liskov gate applies element refinement rules to outputs).

relationships.description: Relationship templates this Class declares — items ARE the flat spec's relationships items ($ref — one shape, single source), and DECLARED CONSUMER-SIDE (a class declares what IT consumes; never who may consume it). Compile: union down the chain, identity = `name` else (edge_type, target, target_field), NEAREST class wins on a redeclare. Liskov (maintainer ruling 2026-08-03 — tighten at your scope): a child MAY redeclare an ancestor's edge to TIGHTEN it — cardinality min may rise, max may fall, enforcement may tighten advisory→structural — never loosen, never retarget, never change edge_type.

immutable.description: Dot-paths into the compiled `spec` that are createOnly. Compile: union down the chain, sorted. OWN-TIER ONLY (maintainer ruling 2026-08-03 — tighten at your scope, never above): each path's head segment MUST name an element DECLARED AT THIS class; freezing inherited surface is reaching above your scope and is a Liskov violation.

context.description: The human-orientation block — IS the flat spec's `context` ($ref — one shape). Permitted ONLY on a `type`-tier Class (#323: prose has one audience-facing home; TYPE-CATALOG renders from it); compile copies it verbatim. Base and provider tiers carry no context (enforced by the allOf conditional + the Liskov gate).

constituents.description: COMPOSITE DEFINITION (the combining artifact, maintainer ruling 2026-08-03): a class MAY compose other classes — items ARE the catalog item's constituents shape ($ref — one shape, one semantic checker: component_id uniqueness, sibling resolution, acyclic depends_on, binding⊆depends_on). Constituent resource_type references resolve in the one dotted namespace (a class or a flat type during migration). Permitted on type and provider tiers (a provider-registered composite is §8.3's case), never base. Constituents do NOT enter the compiled flat spec — a composite EXPANDS at request time; the catalog item is a projection rendered implementation-side (DCM, per-org curation + tenancy), never authored beside the class (one declaration, two projections: registration presents it, the catalog offers it).

then.description: A Base Class has no parent.
A Type/Provider Class MUST name its parent.

shared_data_element.title: SharedDataElement
shared_data_element.description: The composable unit of the Class hierarchy (ADR-038 §2): a data element + its value vocabulary, held at a Class scope. 'Base field', 'shared vocabulary', and 'provider extension' collapse into one shape distinguished only by `scope`. The element `schema` is a declarative JSON-Schema fragment (T1 — data, never executable behavior); `values` are reference-data (ADR-012), the element curated `proposed → canonical`.

element.description: The element name — a lowercase field name in the compiled spec's properties (`cpu`, `memory`, `encryption`). Unique within its owning Class.

scope.description: The Class scope this element is held at, as the dotted Class name. The scope position IS the element's portability (ADR-038 §3) — no separate declaration. MUST equal the owning Class's `resource_type`; the standalone field lets an element be addressed, diffed, and promoted across scopes.

schema.description: The element's declarative shape, a JSON-Schema 2020-12 fragment (the value under the element's key in the compiled spec's `properties`). Declarative constraints only (type/enum/bounds/if-then/pattern) — never executable behavior (T1/T3).

values.description: Optional — declares that this element's values are a GOVERNED vocabulary (ADR-012 reference-data of the named kind), not an inline enum. The element names the vocabulary KIND; the canonical terms are reference-data records of that kind (curated proposed → canonical). Whether an instance MAY supply a bare literal or MUST resolve to a canonical term (a `data_reference`, ADR-012) is a PROFILE floor (ADR-007) enforced by the vocabulary-intake ladder (ADR-039 — match/mint, strict-profile-unknown-refused) — NOT a field here: homelab may write a bare string, sovereign must reference a canonical term.

reference_data_type.description: The reference_data kind that governs this element's values (e.g. `storage_tier`, `os_image`, `vm_size`). Reference-data records of this kind hold the canonical terms; an instance binds one by `data_reference`. Never an inline enum in `schema` for a vocabulary that wants independent curation.

state.description: Curation state (ADR-038 §2): `proposed` — authored, not yet blessed for portable reliance; `canonical` — curated into the shared library. Promotion (proposed→canonical, or lower scope→higher) is the ADR-038 governed contribution operation, visible in diffs.

optional.description: Whether the element is optional at its scope (ADR-014 optionality-with-conformity).

description.description: Cold-reader prose: what the element models and how a provider naturalizes it (DOC-001).
